requirements.title: L editing uses a logical effective item and G editing may edit logical data
requirements.definition: The Lw edit descriptor occupies w positions and its corresponding effective item shall be logical; G editing is also permitted for logical data.

pending.nonlogical-L-item-invalid: Negative source shape: WRITE(buf,'(L1)') 1; repair to a logical item .true. Only the effective-item type differs, and no fixed diagnostic text or phase is asserted.

S13.7.3-001 logical-editing runtime fixtures: two complete internal-file positive-control programs discharge selected L and G logical facets. WRITE(field,'(L2)') .true. expects exactly ' T', proving L editing with a logical effective item. WRITE(field,'(G0)') .false. expects exactly 'F ' in a length-2 internal file by the 13.7.5.3 G0-as-L1 dependency; the length-2 file makes the selected width observable because legal L2 writes ' F'. C1306 keeps L0 outside this unit: w may be zero only for I, B, O, Z, D, E, EN, ES, EX, F, and G, and w is positive for L. Descriptor substitutions L2->L1 and G0->L2 are conforming on logical items, load-bearing on the selected data, and fail.

requirements.title: Logical input standard forms and processor latitude for nonstandard forms
requirements.definition: A logical input field has optional blanks, optional period, T or F, and ignored following characters; a nonstandard form causes an error only if it is not acceptable to the processor.

pending.nonstandard-acceptable-or-error-unassert: Do not file a portable negative for input such as 'YES': the source permits a processor either to accept a nonstandard form or to signal an error if it is not acceptable.

S13.7.3-002 logical-input runtime fixtures: two complete internal READ programs use targets initialized to the opposite logical value and guard-checked before READ. Field ' .Txx' with L5 expects .true.; the leading blank, optional period, T, and ignored trailing characters are all within p2's standard form. Field '   F' with L4 expects .false. after optional leading blanks and F. The fixture also reads a following one-character standard true field solely to make the conforming L4->L3 width mutant deterministic: if the three-blank first field is rejected, IOSTAT is nonzero; if a processor accepts it as an extension, the following L1 field reads F rather than the parent's T and the boundary check fails. Descriptor substitutions L5->L2 and L4->L3 are load-bearing, and every input target has remove/expected sentinel-init probes.

requirements.title: Lowercase logical input letters are equivalent to uppercase
requirements.definition: A lowercase logical input letter is equivalent to the corresponding uppercase letter.

S13.7.3-003 lowercase logical-input runtime fixtures: two complete internal READ programs guard opposite-value logical sentinels before READ. Field ' t' with L2 expects .true. and field '.f' with L2 expects .false., proving lowercase letters are equivalent to uppercase in logical input fields. The lowercase-t descriptor substitution L2->L1 removes the decisive lowercase letter. The lowercase-f fixture also reads a following one-character standard true field solely to make the conforming L2->L1 width mutant deterministic: if the period-only first field is rejected, IOSTAT is nonzero; if a processor accepts it as an extension, the following L1 field reads f rather than the parent's t and the boundary check fails. The expected-value sentinel-init probes fail before READ.
